system.name: SafeVLA (Integrated Safety Approach, ISA)
system.one_liner: Integrated Safety Approach: model safety tasks, elicit unsafe behaviours in a simulator, constrain VLA policies with CMDP-based safe RL, and assure safety with targeted tests.
domain: robot manipulation and navigation in simulation

content.variant_note: four lettered rounded panels laid out as a bent chain (A down to B, B up to C, C right to D) with dotted hand-offs and Update loops, plus code snippets at the right
content.argues: VLA safety needs an integrated approach: model safety-critical task aspects, elicit unsafe behaviours, constrain learning with a CMDP, and assure the resulting policy with targeted evaluations.
content.subject: Four lettered panels (modeling, eliciting, constraining, assuring) linked by dotted hand-offs, plus code snippets of safety predicates.

elements.name: (A) Modeling Safety
elements.role: panel that formalises the safety task
elements.drawn_as: grey rounded panel with bold lettered title

elements.name: Safety-Fetch / Safety-PickUp / Safety-ObjNav
elements.role: the safety task environments modelled in the paper
elements.drawn_as: three light green rounded boxes joined by dashed green double-headed arrows to a junction

elements.name: Modeling Task  t_i = (e_i, x_i, q_i, G, Φ, Ψ)
elements.role: a safety task as a tuple of categories, positions, orientations, objects and two sets of safety predicates
elements.drawn_as: lavender box holding a formula

elements.name: (B) Eliciting Risks
elements.role: panel that rolls the policy out in a simulator to elicit unsafe behaviour
elements.drawn_as: wide grey rounded panel with bold lettered title

elements.name: for categories e_i / for positions x_i / for orientations q_i / for objects G
elements.role: components of the task tuple that parameterise the simulated scene
elements.drawn_as: four lavender boxes down the left side, each tied to a vertical spine by a purple dashed double-headed arrow

elements.name: AI2THOR Simulator
elements.role: environment in which the policy is rolled out
elements.drawn_as: tall blue rounded box

elements.name: h_t = (o_{t+1-H}, a_{t+1-H}, ..., o_t)
elements.role: window of recent observations and actions given to the policy
elements.drawn_as: pink box with a formula, light blue arrow down to the policy

elements.name: Policy π_θi
elements.role: the current VLA policy acting in the simulator, with the instruction l
elements.drawn_as: teal node-and-edge network glyph with orange edges

elements.name: Instruction l / a_t
elements.role: language instruction into the policy and the action out of it back to the simulator
elements.drawn_as: two small pink boxes beside the policy, light blue arrows

elements.name: Trajectories  D = {τ^(n)}_{n=1}^N
elements.role: rollouts collected from the simulator
elements.drawn_as: pink box with a formula

elements.name: Safety Critical Components
elements.role: store of safety predicates: φ_corner(s,a), ψ_blind spot(τ), ψ_fragile collection(τ), ψ_critical point(τ), φ_dangerous equipment(s,a)
elements.drawn_as: pale blue cylinder listing predicate symbols

elements.name: for state-action safety predicates Φ / for trajectory-level safety predicates Ψ
elements.role: slots for the two kinds of predicates that fill the safety critical components
elements.drawn_as: two lavender boxes at the bottom with a purple dashed line up to the cylinder

elements.name: def phi_corner(s, a) / def phi_dangerous_equipment(s, a)
elements.role: predicates implemented as Python-style code returning SAFE or UNSAFE
elements.drawn_as: two blue rounded boxes of 3 pt monospace code tied to the cylinder by dashed leaders, an ellipsis between them

elements.name: Update
elements.role: feedback from the safety components back to the task components for the next round; content not explained
elements.drawn_as: dashed black arrows along the bottom of panel B with the word Update

elements.name: (C) Constraining Policies
elements.role: panel that turns trajectories into costs and rewards and defines the constrained problem
elements.drawn_as: grey rounded panel with bold lettered title

elements.name: Cost Function / Reward Function
elements.role: compute per-trajectory costs {c_i(τ^(n))} and rewards {r(τ^(n), l)}
elements.drawn_as: pale yellow boxes with set-builder formulas

elements.name: Costs / Rewards
elements.role: the computed cost and reward sets passed to the CMDP
elements.drawn_as: pink boxes with formulas, black arrows to the cylinder

elements.name: CMDP
elements.role: constrained problem: max over θ of J_r(θ) subject to J_{C_i}(θ) ≤ 0 for every cost i
elements.drawn_as: tan cylinder holding the objective

elements.name: (D) Safety Assurance
elements.role: panel of targeted safety evaluations on the way to the next policy
elements.drawn_as: grey rounded panel with thick black outline

elements.name: Test-time Safety / Long-tail Safety / Extreme Failure Safety
elements.role: three assurance checks
elements.drawn_as: three light teal rounded boxes stacked

elements.name: Policy π_θ_{i+1}
elements.role: the next, safer policy
elements.drawn_as: teal network glyph at the far right behind a large teal arrow

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw a multi-aspect pipeline as lettered grey panels, using thick dotted arrows for hand-offs between panels and thin solid arrows inside them; show a store of components as a cylinder and tie real code boxes to it with dashed leaders.
lessons.suits: Safety, alignment or RL pipelines that combine task modelling, data elicitation, a constrained objective and an evaluation stage, where formulas and code carry part of the story.

evidence: We argue that VLA safety requires an integrated safety approach (ISA), rather than a single method.
(i) modeling safety-critical aspects of tasks and environments; (ii) eliciting latent and diverse unsafe behaviors from existing policies;
(iii) constraining the VLA’s learning process to integrate these safety considerations; and (iv) assuring the resulting model’s safety

summary: SafeVLA proposes an Integrated Safety Approach (ISA) for aligning vision-language-action models with safety constraints. Figure 1 draws the pipeline as four lettered rounded grey panels: (A) Modeling Safety, with three safety task boxes and a task tuple; (B) Eliciting Risks, where task components configure an AI2THOR simulator in which the policy acts, trajectories are collected, and a cylinder of safety predicates is tied by dashed leaders to two Python-style code snippets; (C) Constraining Policies, where cost and reward functions feed a CMDP cylinder with a max-subject-to-constraints objective; and (D) Safety Assurance, three tests leading to the next policy, shown as a network glyph. Dotted, dashed, light blue and teal arrows separate kinds of flow, and formulas fill many boxes.
summary_zh: SafeVLA 提出集成安全方法（ISA）。图 1 用 A 到 D 四个灰色圆角面板画流程：建模安全任务；在 AI2THOR 中引出风险并收集轨迹；用代价与奖励构成 CMDP 约束策略；三类测试保证安全；右侧附两段谓词代码。
notes: The roles of the Update arrows, of the purple dashed double-headed arrows and of the exact hand-over from the CMDP through the teal funnel into panel D are read from the drawing and the four aspects named in the paper, not explained in the caption. The prior kind (stage-pipeline) is kept as the only kind; the formulas and the simulator loop are parts of the stages.
